title: Fitting Words and Self-Control
overview: A second collection of Solomon's sayings, gathered under King Hezekiah, offers practical wisdom about rulers, speech, restraint and how to treat neighbors and even enemies.

parts.label: Kings and hidden things (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Scribes at King Hezekiah's court, about two centuries after Solomon, gathered these sayings. God is honored for depths we cannot reach, while a good king is honored for looking into matters carefully and removing corrupt advisers, the way a silversmith burns impurities out of silver before shaping it.

parts.label: Humility and lawsuits (vv. 6-10)
parts.note: Do not push yourself forward at court, since being invited up is better than being sent down in public, an idea Jesus echoes in a story about banquet seating (Luke 14). Try to settle a dispute with your neighbor directly instead of rushing to court, and do not reveal someone's secret to win, because the shame will land on you.

parts.label: Words that fit (vv. 11-15)
parts.note: A well-timed word is as lovely as golden fruit set in silver, probably a decorative piece people then knew, and wise correction is worth more than gold jewelry to someone willing to hear it. A reliable messenger refreshes like a drink cooled with mountain snow at harvest, a person who promises gifts and never gives them is like clouds that bring no rain, and patient, gentle speech can wear down even stubborn resistance.

parts.label: Too much, and no care (vv. 16-20)
parts.note: Good things turn sour in excess, honey and frequent visits alike. A false witness wounds like a weapon, an unreliable person fails you like a broken tooth when you lean on them, and cheerful songs sung to a grieving person only deepen the hurt.

parts.label: Feeding your enemy (vv. 21-22)
parts.note: Meet an enemy's hunger and thirst with food and water. The burning coals most likely stand for the sting of shame or a change of heart that kindness can stir, though scholars are not certain, and Christians read these lines, which Paul quotes in Romans 12, alongside Jesus' call to love enemies.

parts.label: Closing pictures (vv. 23-28)
parts.note: Gossip stirs up anger as surely as wind brings rain, and living on a corner of a flat roof beats sharing a house with constant quarreling, a saying aimed at the men of its day. Good news from far away refreshes, a good person who gives in to the wicked is like a muddied spring, and someone without self-control is as exposed as a city with broken walls.

think: Can you remember a time when a word spoken at just the right moment, or the wrong one, changed how you saw something?
